sections.label: 1. Overview
sections.title: 1. Overview
body: Ownward Hub (“Ownward,” “we,” “our,” or “us”) provides tools and services to help users run, grow, buy, and sell businesses. This Privacy Policy explains how we collect, use, disclose, and protect personal information when you use our websites, applications, and related services (collectively, the “Services”).

sections.label: 2. Information We Collect
sections.title: 2. Information We Collect
bullets: Information you provide: account details, profile information, contact form content, uploaded documents, and communications.
Transaction and service data: records related to subscriptions, billing interactions, and use of product features.
Technical data: device, browser, IP address, log and diagnostics data, and security telemetry.
Privacy settings data: your selected privacy choices, including consent preferences stored in your browser.

sections.label: 3. How We Use Information
sections.title: 3. How We Use Information
bullets: Provide, operate, and improve the Services.
Authenticate users, maintain account security, and prevent fraud or abuse.
Process requests, support inquiries, and other communications.
Comply with legal obligations and enforce our terms.
Operate optional functionality and analytics technologies only where permitted.

sections.label: 4. Legal Bases for Processing
sections.title: 4. Legal Bases for Processing
body: Depending on your location, we may process personal information based on contract necessity, legitimate interests, legal obligations, and consent where required.

sections.label: 5. How We Share Information
sections.title: 5. How We Share Information
body: We may share personal information with:
bullets: Service providers that host infrastructure, support authentication, and process payments.
Professional advisors and authorities where required by law.
Parties involved in a merger, acquisition, financing, or other corporate transaction.

sections.label: 6. Cookies and Local Storage
sections.title: 6. Cookies and Local Storage
body: Necessary storage supports authentication, security, requested workflows, and your privacy-choice record. Optional categories (functionality and analytics) remain disabled unless you permit them.

sections.label: 7. Data Retention
sections.title: 7. Data Retention
body: We retain personal information for as long as needed to provide Services, meet legal obligations, resolve disputes, and enforce agreements.

sections.label: 8. Data Security
sections.title: 8. Data Security
body: We use administrative, technical, and physical safeguards designed to protect personal information. No method of transmission or storage is fully secure, and we cannot guarantee absolute security.

sections.label: 9. Your Privacy Rights and Choices
sections.title: 9. Your Privacy Rights and Choices
body: Depending on applicable law, you may have rights to access, correct, delete, restrict, object to, or export personal information. You may also update optional privacy preferences at any time.

sections.label: 10. International Data Transfers
sections.title: 10. International Data Transfers
body: We may process information in countries other than your own and apply safeguards as required by applicable law.

sections.label: 11. Children’s Privacy
sections.title: 11. Children’s Privacy
body: The Services are not directed to children under 13 (or higher age where required by local law), and we do not knowingly collect personal information from children.

sections.label: 12. Changes to This Policy
sections.title: 12. Changes to This Policy
body: We may update this Privacy Policy from time to time. Material changes will be posted with an updated effective date and last-updated date.

UrgencyTriage.heading: Is this actually urgent?
UrgencyTriage.description: Answer four questions to identify what kind of response this situation actually requires.

questions.q1: Is someone in immediate danger, or are there new or severe physical symptoms that may require urgent medical attention?
questions.q2: Is there a real external deadline within the next 24 hours with a material consequence?
questions.q3: Is the decision difficult to reverse, expensive, public, contractual, or likely to affect another person significantly?
questions.q4: Can you preserve your options by communicating, requesting time, delegating, or taking a smaller temporary action?

protect.title: Protect
protect.message: Safety or immediate health is the priority. Address that first before considering anything else.

preserve.title: Preserve
preserve.message: A real deadline exists. Identify specifically what happens if you miss it, and decide based on that information.

create-decision-space.title: Create decision space
create-decision-space.message: This decision carries weight. You have time to slow down, gather information, and make a more considered choice.

schedule.title: Schedule
schedule.message: This does not require an immediate response. Schedule a time to address it when you are in a better position to think clearly.

appendMessages.option-preserving: You have identified a way to preserve options. Use that step before making the larger decision.
appendMessages.identify-help: The next useful step may be to identify who has the authority, knowledge, or capacity to help.

intro.title: Business Idea Readiness Check
intro.description: Take the free Business Idea Readiness Check. In a few minutes, identify what is clear, what is missing, and what you should do next.
intro.privacyStatement: Your answers are never made public and no personal information is requested. With functionality consent enabled, your progress is saved across page refreshes. Without consent, everything stays in memory only.

controls.restartConfirm: Are you sure you want to restart? Your current answers will be cleared.

validation.selectAnswer: Please select an answer to continue.

q1.text: How clearly can you describe the specific problem your idea solves?

options.not_yet: I have not defined a problem yet
options.general_idea: I have a general idea of the problem
options.clear: I can describe the problem clearly
options.validated: I have confirmed the problem with real people

q2.text: How well do you understand why this problem matters to the people who experience it?

options.not_yet: I have not explored this yet
options.general_idea: I have some guesses about why it matters
options.validated: People have told me directly how much it affects them

q3.text: How clearly have you defined who your target customer is?

options.general_idea: I have a broad category in mind
options.clear: I have a specific profile with key traits
options.validated: I have spoken with real people who match the profile

q4.text: How well do you understand how your target customer currently deals with this problem?

options.not_yet: I have not looked into this
options.clear: I understand their current workarounds or alternatives
options.validated: I have direct evidence from conversations or research

q5.text: How clearly defined is your product or service offering?

options.clear: I can describe what I would deliver
options.validated: I have a specific offer I have tested or described to potential customers

q6.text: How clear is your understanding of why a customer would choose your offer over alternatives?

options.not_yet: I have not thought about this yet
options.general_idea: I have a rough sense of the advantage
options.clear: I can articulate a clear differentiation
options.validated: Potential customers have confirmed this advantage matters to them

q7.text: How clear is your plan for how you will charge for your product or service?

options.general_idea: I have a rough pricing idea
options.clear: I have a specific pricing model in mind
options.validated: I have tested or discussed pricing with potential customers

q8.text: How well do you understand the economics required for your idea to be financially sustainable?

options.clear: I have estimated basic costs and required revenue
options.validated: I have modeled the numbers and they appear viable

q9.text: How clear is your immediate next step to move this idea forward?

options.not_yet: I am not sure what to do next
options.general_idea: I have a general sense of the next step
options.clear: I know my next concrete action
options.validated: I have a specific plan with a timeline

q10.text: How ready are you to commit regular time to this idea over the next 30 days?

options.not_yet: Not able to commit time right now
options.clear: I have a realistic block of time I can protect
options.validated: I have already blocked consistent time and started

q11.text: What is your biggest obstacle right now?

options.not_sure_where_to_start: I am not sure where to start
options.customer_research: Finding and talking to potential customers
options.define_offer: Defining exactly what I will sell
options.technical_help: Technical skills or tools I need

q12.text: How many hours per week can you realistically dedicate to this idea right now?

results.heading: Your Readiness Results

levelDescriptions.idea_discovery: Your idea is at an early stage. The most valuable next steps are to sharpen your understanding of the problem and identify who it affects most.
levelDescriptions.early_validation: You have a foundation in place. Focusing on customer clarity and a defined offer will help you validate whether this idea has real traction.
levelDescriptions.test_ready: You have solid groundwork. The next step is to run a small, low-cost test to see how real customers respond.
levelDescriptions.execution_ready: You are well-prepared to move forward. The focus now is on consistent execution and tracking early results.

summary.idea_discovery: Your answers show this idea is still taking shape. That is a normal starting point. The clearest path forward is to narrow down the problem and the person it affects before anything else.
summary.early_validation: You have a clearer picture than you might think, but there are key gaps to address before committing resources. Your next focus should be direct conversations with potential customers.
summary.test_ready: The groundwork is solid. You have defined the problem, identified the customer, and outlined an offer. The missing piece is real-world validation through a structured small test.
summary.execution_ready: You have done the foundational work well. The challenge now is maintaining momentum and adapting based on early feedback.

whatIsClearItems.customer_clarity: You have a clear picture of who your target customer is.
whatIsClearItems.offer_value: You have defined your offer and understand its value.
whatIsClearItems.business_model: You understand how your business will generate revenue.
whatIsClearItems.execution_readiness: You are ready to take action and move forward.

whatIsMissingItems.problem_clarity: The problem your idea solves is not yet clearly defined or validated.
whatIsMissingItems.customer_clarity: The profile of your target customer still needs more definition.
whatIsMissingItems.offer_value: Your offer and its differentiation need more clarity or validation.
whatIsMissingItems.business_model: The revenue model and financial sustainability need more work.
whatIsMissingItems.execution_readiness: A clear next step and committed time plan are still missing.

results.disclaimer: This score reflects your self-reported preparation based on the answers you provided. It is not a professional evaluation, prediction of business success, or guarantee of any outcome.

recommendations.action_clarify_problem: Write a one-sentence description of the specific problem you are solving and share it with three people who might experience it. Ask them whether it resonates.
recommendations.action_define_customer: Build a one-page customer profile: who they are, what triggers the problem, and how they currently deal with it.
recommendations.action_validate_offer: Describe your offer in plain language and share it with potential customers. Ask if they would use it and what would make them hesitate.
recommendations.action_map_revenue: Sketch a simple business model: what you charge, what it costs to deliver, and how many customers you need to break even.
recommendations.action_build_momentum: Block a recurring time slot this week to work on one specific next action. Start small and protect the time.
recommendations.action_start_framework: Write down your idea in three parts: the problem, who has it, and your proposed solution. Use this as your working foundation.
recommendations.action_customer_research: Identify five people who could be your customer and reach out to schedule a 20-minute conversation this week.
recommendations.action_explore_funding: List the minimum resources you need to test your idea. Separate what you can start with today from what requires funding.
recommendations.action_technical_first_step: Identify the single most important technical capability your idea requires. Find one free resource, course, or person who can help you with it.
recommendations.action_accountability_system: Tell one person about your idea and commit to a specific update in 7 days. Accountability is one of the highest-leverage early tools.
recommendations.action_organize_idea: Spend one hour writing down everything you know about your idea, then group it into: what you know, what you assume, and what you need to find out.
recommendations.action_next_concrete_step: Choose one specific action you can complete this week that moves your idea forward. Write it down and schedule it.

immediateActions.immediate_problem_clarity: Write a one-sentence problem statement today and share it with one person who might experience the problem.
immediateActions.immediate_customer_clarity: List three specific people you know who could represent your target customer. Send one of them a message today.
immediateActions.immediate_offer_value: Write down your offer in one sentence: who it is for, what it delivers, and what makes it different from alternatives.
immediateActions.immediate_business_model: Estimate the price you would charge, the main cost to deliver it, and how many customers you would need in month one.
immediateActions.immediate_execution_readiness: Block 30 minutes today to define your one most important next action and schedule it.

problem_clarity.day1: Write a rough draft of the problem you are trying to solve in one or two sentences.
problem_clarity.day2: List five specific people who might experience this problem.
problem_clarity.day3: Reach out to two people from your list and ask for a 15-minute conversation.
problem_clarity.day4: Conduct your first conversation. Focus on listening, not pitching.
problem_clarity.day5: Conduct your second conversation and compare what you heard.
problem_clarity.day6: Rewrite your problem statement based on what you learned.
problem_clarity.day7: Share your updated problem statement with one more person and ask if it resonates.

customer_clarity.day1: Write a rough customer profile: who they are, their age or role, and what triggers the problem.
customer_clarity.day2: List five specific people or communities where your customer type congregates.
customer_clarity.day3: Reach out to two people who match the profile and ask for a brief conversation.
customer_clarity.day4: Hold your first conversation. Ask about their experience with the problem, not your solution.
customer_clarity.day5: Hold your second conversation. Focus on what surprised you.
customer_clarity.day6: Refine your customer profile based on what you heard.
customer_clarity.day7: Write a one-paragraph description of your target customer and share it with someone for feedback.

offer_value.day1: Write a simple description of what you will sell, who it is for, and what outcome it delivers.
offer_value.day2: List three to five alternatives a customer could use instead of your offer.
offer_value.day3: Write one sentence explaining why your offer is different or better.
offer_value.day4: Share your offer description with two potential customers and ask for honest feedback.
offer_value.day5: Revise your offer based on what you heard.
offer_value.day6: Write down the top objection a customer might have and how you would respond.
offer_value.day7: Finalize a one-paragraph offer summary you could share with anyone.

business_model.day1: Write down your proposed price and the top reason a customer would pay it.
business_model.day2: List the three main costs involved in delivering your offer.
business_model.day3: Calculate how many customers you would need per month to cover basic costs.
business_model.day4: Identify one revenue assumption you are least confident about and test it.
business_model.day5: Ask one potential customer whether your price feels reasonable for the outcome delivered.
business_model.day6: Revise your numbers based on what you learned.
business_model.day7: Write a one-page financial summary: price, key costs, break-even estimate, and confidence level.

execution_readiness.day1: Write down the one action that would move your idea forward the most right now.
execution_readiness.day2: Block recurring time this week dedicated to this idea — at minimum 30 minutes per session.
execution_readiness.day3: Complete the first concrete task you identified on Day 1.
execution_readiness.day4: Identify one person who could give you useful feedback or accountability on your progress.
execution_readiness.day5: Share your current progress with that person and ask for their input.
execution_readiness.day6: Identify the next three actions after today and write them down in order.
execution_readiness.day7: Review what you accomplished this week and set a specific goal for the week ahead.

problem_clarity_not_sure_where_to_start_.day1: In 10 minutes, write one sentence about a problem you see that bothers you or others.
problem_clarity_not_sure_where_to_start_.day2: Ask yourself: do I personally experience this problem? Does someone I know?
problem_clarity_not_sure_where_to_start_.day3: Send a message to one person who might experience it and ask one open question.
problem_clarity_not_sure_where_to_start_.day4: Read their reply. Note one thing that surprised you.
problem_clarity_not_sure_where_to_start_.day5: Rewrite your problem sentence using what you learned.
problem_clarity_not_sure_where_to_start_.day6: Read it out loud. Does it still feel true?
problem_clarity_not_sure_where_to_start_.day7: Write your clearest version and save it as your starting point.

customer_clarity_customer_research_limit.day1: Write one sentence describing who has the problem you want to solve.
customer_clarity_customer_research_limit.day2: Name one real person you know who fits that description.
customer_clarity_customer_research_limit.day3: Send them a short message asking about their experience.
customer_clarity_customer_research_limit.day4: Read their reply and note the most important thing.
customer_clarity_customer_research_limit.day5: Update your customer description with one new insight.
customer_clarity_customer_research_limit.day6: Identify one more person to speak with next week.
customer_clarity_customer_research_limit.day7: Write a two-sentence customer description you can use as a guide going forward.

execution_readiness_confidence_accountab.day1: Write down the one thing you are most hesitant about.
execution_readiness_confidence_accountab.day2: Choose the smallest possible first step. Something you can do in 15 minutes.
execution_readiness_confidence_accountab.day4: Tell one person what you did.
execution_readiness_confidence_accountab.day5: Ask them to check in with you in two days.
execution_readiness_confidence_accountab.day6: Complete one more small step before the check-in.
execution_readiness_confidence_accountab.day7: Have the check-in. Decide on your next step for next week.
